comments.body:
one interesting point to bring up is that this design is implicitly guiding module authors to craft process args in a very specific way: daemons which require a restart on configuration change will directly include path to the nix store in args, daemons which allow a reload instead will use this new config data mechanism

there is no problem here with finit service manager, for example, because it is very compatible with systemd in that any change to argv will automatically cause a restart... and there is a mechanism like the `reloadTriggers` to force reloads on configuration change 👍

but i wonder if this can have implications on other service managers? 🤔 i am not sure how actionable these points are... just thought i would bring them up as a point of discussion

Thank you @aanderse.

> very compatible with systemd in that any change to argv will automatically cause a restart...

I suspect that service managers that do not natively operate this way can be made to do so with a wrapper, but I don't have proof. Alternatively, doing a restart instead of a reload is perhaps acceptable for a less capable service manager.

> `reloadTriggers`

Let's do those in a separate PR. I've checked nix-processmgmt, and it doesn't [seem](https://github.com/svanderburg/nix-processmgmt/blob/master/nixproc/backends/systemd/generate-systemd-service.nix) to handle this aspect, so maybe this requires some tinkering, or more likely we should just have it and see if it causes problems for service managers other than systemd and finit.

Anyway, I didn't plan to implement this on my own until I realized we don't really have much of an established pattern for this kind of thing yet and it wouldn't be trivial. Now we have an example.

Also we should really expand the contributor base for this stuff. Would you like to implement the `reloadTriggers` option?

looked over the code, this seems helpful

a `reloadTriggers` option would pair with this well... otherwise module authors have to choose between "hard restart on config change" vs "never restart or reload on config change"

maybe this can be added in a future PR
